source_issue.title: PR interactions: pagination stops early, so CMFPlone and Volto get 0 rows for past years

summary_markdown:
## What this issue is about
This issue addresses a bug in the `plone_pr_interactions.py` script. Currently, it retrieves pull requests (PRs) sorted by their last update date and stops early if it encounters an empty page, leading to inaccurate activity reports for older years in the Plone ecosystem, specifically for `CMFPlone` and `Volto`.

## What needs to be done
1. Modify the pagination logic to continue fetching PRs as long as there are updates after the target date range.
2. Change the filtering criteria to use the PR's creation or merge date instead of the last updated date.
3. Recollect the data for all years to ensure accurate statistics.

## Helpful background
This issue is tagged as a normal priority bug and is considered easy to work on. It affects how PR interactions are reported, influencing the statistics visible in `reports/github-pr-interactions-report-*.md`.

## Good first steps
1. Familiarize yourself with the `plone_pr_interactions.py` file, particularly around line 197.
2. Understand pagination and how the current logic stops prematurely.
3. Consider how to implement the suggested changes and test them to confirm they work as expected.
4. You may want to coordinate with others on potential approaches if you encounter any ambiguity.
